subject: nahw
definition: What is said about the mubtadaʾ, completing the meaning of the nominal sentence. It is marfūʿ.
explanation: In زَيْدٌ قَائِمٌ, qāʾimun is the khabar: it tells what Zayd is. The khabar can be a single word, a sentence (زَيْدٌ قَامَ أَبُوهُ, Zayd, his father stood) or a phrase (زَيْدٌ فِي الدَّارِ, Zayd is in the house).
A single-word khabar is usually indefinite and agrees with the mubtadaʾ in number and gender: الطَّالِبَانِ مُجْتَهِدَانِ (the two students are diligent).

examples.english: Zayd is in the house: a phrase as khabar.
The two students are diligent: the khabar agrees in number.
